pick.name: Electron (+ Vite React renderer sharing packages/ui with web)
pick.why: In-process Node runs the AI-agent stack directly (Claude Agent SDK, MCP stdio servers, node-llama-cpp, onnxruntime-node, Playwright); same Chromium on every OS; biggest ecosystem (7.6M/wk)

alts.name: Tauri 2
alts.what: Rust shell + system WebView (WebView2 on Windows)
alts.why: Installers of a few MB and lower RAM; strong permission model

alts.name: Electrobun
alts.what: TS desktop apps: Bun main process + system webview (optional CEF)
alts.why: TS-only like Electron with Tauri-like size and built-in kilobyte delta updates

candidates.name: Electron (pick)
candidates.verdict: Best for AI-agent desktop apps that need Node in-process; cost is ~100MB+ installers and RAM.

candidates.name: Tauri 2
candidates.verdict: Wins when small download/RAM matters and the app is mostly UI; Node-based AI tools need a sidecar binary; Rust is a second language.

candidates.name: Electrobun
candidates.verdict: Promising Electron-alternative in pure TS; young ecosystem, Bun-vs-Node native addon compatibility to test.

candidates.name: Wails v3 (Go)
candidates.verdict: v3.0.0 stable 2026-10-26; Go backend - extra language, mobile experimental.

candidates.name: Flutter desktop
candidates.verdict: Good if Flutter is the mobile pick; no React reuse.

candidates.name: Avalonia 12 / .NET MAUI / WinUI
candidates.verdict: C# stacks; no web code reuse.

decision: Electron is the pick because AI-agent features on device are first-class in Node (Agent SDK, MCP servers, local models) and the renderer reuses the web React code unchanged. Switch to Tauri 2 for lightweight utilities where a ~5-10MB installer matters, and re-evaluate Electrobun in 2027.
details: Migration cost: none if your existing desktop app is Electron; keep any .NET sidecar as a child process. Harden with contextIsolation, sandbox, @electron/fuses.

verify.note: Stress-tested: Electron holds for an agent-heavy app. MCP stdio servers, Playwright, node-llama-cpp and onnxruntime-node all need a Node runtime; Tauri's official route is a per-target-triple sidecar binary compiled with pkg, short-lived per call, with long-lived IPC left to you. Caveat: the Claude Agent SDK itself 'runs the Claude Code binary' as a subprocess, so for that item Electron's edge is smaller than the 'why' implies.
